transitions.summary: Wording modernisation only (v0 LON-063 -> v1 GLD1-EN004): 'Offer 1 monster on your side of the field as a Tribute (excluding this monster). Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster Card from your Fusion Deck.' becomes 'Tribute 1 other monster to Special Summon 1 Fusion Monster from your Fusion Deck.' Both keep the pre-PSCT 'Tribute X to do Y' construction that the era ruled as a cost, and both keep the end-of-turn destruction of the Summoned Fusion Monster.

transitions.summary: Functional erratum: the Tribute moved from a cost to part of the resolution. The goat script pays it as a cost - e1:SetCost(s.cost) using Duel.CheckReleaseGroupCost / Duel.SelectReleaseGroupCost / Duel.Release(g,REASON_COST) - so the FLIP effect cannot even activate unless a Tributable monster AND a Summonable Fusion Monster both exist, and the Tribute is paid even if the effect is subsequently negated. The modern script's target function returns true unconditionally and performs Duel.SelectReleaseGroup / Duel.Release(rg,REASON_EFFECT) inside the operation, matching v2's PSCT 'Tribute 1 other monster, and if you do, Special Summon ...', so the effect activates regardless and simply does nothing on resolution if the Tribute cannot be made. Upstream annotates the variant 'tributing monster is a cost'.

rulings_check.difference: Era Summoner of Illusions pays the Tribute as a cost when the effect is activated (paid even if the effect is then negated); modern Tributes on resolution ('Tribute 1 other monster, and if you do, Special Summon ...'). Because the Tribute is a cost, the era effect cannot be activated unless a Summonable Fusion Monster exists (and a monster to Tribute); the modern effect activates regardless and simply does nothing if it cannot resolve.

review.notes:
Baseline goat/c504700184.lua matches lineage v0 (LON-063, Labyrinth of Nightmare, 2003-03-01) exactly. Both target eras fall before the v2 erratum (GOAT 2005-04-01 and Edison 2010-04-24 are both earlier than 2012-09-29), so both take the goat variant. Trailing cosmetic rewording v2 -> v3 (FUEN-EN038, 2017-02-23, '. Destroy that Fusion Monster during the End Phase of this turn' -> ', but destroy it during the End Phase of this turn'; v3 is the pinned modern text) is not recorded as a change. The classification is functional rather than cosmetic despite the transition being a PSCT rewording, because the script diff carries positive evidence of a resolution difference (SetCost vs an in-resolution Release) rather than mere formalisation; the remaining diff items - CATEGORY_RELEASE on the modern effect, where s.rfilter is defined, and RESETS_STANDARD_PHASE_END vs its expanded spelling - are hint-only or identical.

Round 037 (2026-09-29). Checked against period rulings: the differences the functional transition claims were searched for in the Konami-hosted UDE card FAQ (2008-12), the 2005 UDE card rulings page, Konami's errata lists, rulebooks and per-set ruling documents, and the archived UDE judge-list threads Yugipedia points to (the transition's rulings_check; docs/research/text-only-errata-audit.md, Summoner of Illusions). The rulings read support d1, d2 at both snapshots (the passages are in the check); nothing contradicts a claimed difference, so kind, summary and coverage are unchanged. Verdicts: [c1] d1 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu; d2 supported at Edison, supported at Tengu.
